a-file-may-also.fe4d: A file may also name itself, with a title: line above the first entry — title: Circuits for Lesson 1 of the Tutorial. That title is what the interface shows in place of the filename, and it is what the supplied examples are listed by. A file without one is shown by its filename instead.
a-general-tidy-up.13d3: A general tidy-up. Tries several routes and keeps whichever comes out shortest, so it is the one to reach for first and the least predictable.
a-plain-text-input.ab74: A plain text input file holds as many entries as you like. An entry is one set of inputs to be solved together: a circuit, the analysis to run on it, and the settings to run it with. Each starts with its name in square brackets, followed by the element lines and then its settings. The file extension is .cir.
a-transient-tr-solve.a88c: A transient (TR) solve hands over its answers as functions of time, with t as a Known you can set — or make t the Unknown and find when a waveform reaches a value.
a-value-can-be.5443: A value can be a number, a symbol (r_load, vin) or an expression — and an expression referring to another answer, like 2*v_2, makes a dependent (controlled) source.
about-input-file-cir.e152: About input file (.cir) formatAbout the .cir format
add-conditions-one-per.9e8f: Add conditions — one per line or separated by and, e.g. pr1 > 0 and v1 = 12; use >= and <=, not => and =<
add-equations-one-per.a132: Add equations — one per line or separated by and, e.g. v_2 = 6 and p_e1=10; parsed the same as circuit values — SI shorthand like 4.7'k and, in AC, imaginary units (i/j) both work, but a bare suffix like 4.7k with no apostrophe doesn't
add-unknowns-one-per.ac15: Add unknowns — one per line or separated by commas, e.g. vx or v_x
an-answer-arrives-arranged.8518: An answer arrives arranged the way the solver happened to leave it, which is not always the way you want to read it. These rearrange it without changing what it is. Wrap the answer's name in one: expand(vo) rather than plain vo.
an-fd-solve-hands.4221: An FD solve hands over its s-domain system, with s as a Known complex number you can move around the plane.
an-interactive-numerical-sol.9a63: An interactive numerical solver to explore your circuit's equations and variables. Arrives preloaded with the solved circuit's equation system and results — untick an equation, flip a Known to Unknown, and see how the results change.
and-e-all-mean.0bae: 8000, 8000. and 8E3 all mean the same number; the last two are read as approximate rather than exact.
angular-frequency-rad-s.308a: ω — angular frequency (rad/s, number or symbol)
bode-plot-of-transfer.445b: Bode plot of transfer function H(s)
case-matters-here-m.5402: Case matters here. 'M is mega and 'm is milli — a factor of a billion apart. (Both 'k and 'K mean kilo.) Micro accepts either u or µ, so a value pasted from a datasheet works as typed. There is no prefix for exa: a bare E glued directly to digits, like 8E3, is read as scientific notation instead — see below for when E/e mean that versus an ordinary variable.
conditions-one-per-line.690b: Conditions — one per line or separated by and, e.g. pr1 > 0 and v1 = 12; use >= and <=, not => and =<
conditions-one-per-line.bc4e: Conditions — one per line or separated by and, e.g. t = to, which substitutes a value before evaluating, the way the calculator's | does; pr1 > 0 states an assumption. Use >= and <=, not => and =<
describe-a-circuit-and.ff60: Describe a circuit and select analysis type — You can use an Input File.
do-you-want-to.c926: Do you want to limit the results to save time?
double-click-start-command.8ded: double-click start.command (the first time, right-click it and choose “Open” — macOS blocks downloaded scripts by default)
download-the-input-file.ae7b: Download the input file as it now stands
draw-the-circuit-above.4fac: Draw the circuit above as a diagram (beta)
e-e-only-mean.6faa: E/e only mean scientific notation when glued directly onto digits with no space or operator in between — 1E3 and 1e3 both mean 1000. Written on their own (E, e), or separated from a number by *, they are ordinary variables like any other: 1*E3 and 1*e3 mean "1 times the variable named E3 / e3", not "1 times E times 3".
empty-every-input-and.02e4: Empty every input and start over
equation-s-to-solve.70c0: Equation(s) to solve in terms of the results — one per line or separated by and, e.g. v2 = 6 or v_2 = 6
evaluate-an-expression-in.2dbf: Evaluate an expression in terms of the results — e.g. pr1 + pr2 or p_r1 + p_r2; several SymPy functions allowed (see below)
everything-after-the-element.afbf: Everything after the element lines is optional, and can be left out entirely — leaving a key out just means the app's own default applies, same as if you'd never touched it: analysis (dc/ac/fd/tr), omega, variables, tool (th/er/port) with n1/n2/kind, note (text of your own, shown when the entry is loaded — repeat the line for a second paragraph), image (a link to a picture of the circuit, shown above the description when the entry is loaded — a web address, or a path relative to this page; a picture on your own computer cannot be linked to, because the browser will not read your files for a web page, and you may cap how wide it is drawn by writing [400px] after the link), and (if the circuit uses it) the expert-mode equations, conditions and unknowns; the Settings rounding (exact/approx/a number of significant digits/exact+n for both at once), si, units, rms and show_equations (each yes/no); and, if you were using them when you saved, evaluate with its own evaluate_conditions, the standalone equation solver's solve_equations / solve_conditions / solve_unknowns / solve_real_only, and the plot tool's plottool (sweep/bode/bode_tf/plot_time) / plotkey / plotx (the variable on the x-axis) / plotmin / plotmax / plotpoints.
exact-and-approx-to.d065: exact and approx to n digits
explore-the-equations-genera.26e9: Explore the equations generated for your circuit with a handy numerical solver.
extract-the-contents-of.a79b: Extract the contents of this file, and run the program for the first time. This is done according to your operating system:
free-and-open-source.dd6c: Free and open-source software under the MIT licence · results are symbolic, powered by SymPy
gain-voltage-current-and.e378: gain — voltage, current and power gain
gathers-the-terms-in.3fd9: Gathers the terms in one symbol — the second argument says which, and it is not optional. r1*v1 + r2*v1 + r3*v2 → r3*v2 + v1*(r1 + r2)
i-n-p-u.3c01: [ I N P U T S ]
if-a-newer-version.2426: If a newer version of Symbulator 9 comes out, download the new ZIP. To install it cleanly, first remove the current app — when uninstalling, check “Remove this app's data from Chrome” — then repeat the install process above with the new ZIP. If you'd rather not reinstall, you can instead try forcing a full reload: press Ctrl+Shift+R (Windows/Linux) or Cmd+Shift+R (Mac) — though a clean reinstall is the more reliable fix.
if-the-button-does.3287: If the button does not appear, give the page a moment and tap it once; browsers wait until you have actually used a page before offering to install it. Failing that, use the browser's own menu — on a phone there is no install icon in the address bar, that being a desktop-only feature. In Chrome on Android, open the browser menu (⋮, top right) and choose the install entry: depending on the version it reads “Install app”, “Install and create shortcut”, or “Add to Home Screen”. On iPhone and iPad, use Safari's Share button and choose “Add to Home Screen”.
in-evaluate-and-solve.a841: In Evaluate and Solve you can refer to any answer with or without its underscore, in any capitalisation — so i_r1, ir1, i_R1 and IR1 all mean the current through r1. Answers are named v_<node> for node voltages and, per element, i_ current, v_ voltage drop, p_ power, s_ complex power, z_/r_ impedance seen by a source.
in-fd-analysis-s.00ed: In FD analysis s is the complex frequency and in TR t is time; elsewhere both are ordinary variables.

once-symbulator-is-open.fd07: Once Symbulator 9 is open in your browser, a bar appears at the top of the page offering to install it — click “Install” and confirm. If you dismissed that bar, or it never appeared, look for an “Install” icon in the address bar instead, or open the browser's menu and choose “Install Symbulator 9”. After installing, it opens like any other app, with no internet needed and no more running start scripts. Once you've finished this first session, you can close that window — the installed app runs on its own from now on.
once-you-ve-installed.132b: Once you've installed it as an app, you can delete the ZIP and the unzipped folder — the installed app now runs entirely from your browser's own storage and won't need them again. It's still worth keeping the ZIP somewhere safe, though, in case you ever need to reinstall (for example, if you clear your browser's site data, switch browsers, or move to a different computer).
one-element-per-line.7c7f: One element per line (or separated by :), fields separated by ,; node 0 is ground. See the documentation for a full walkthrough, or pick an example circuit above to see it in practice.
one-equation-per-line.fb04: one equation per line, e.g.   Vout = Vin * R2 / (R1 + R2)
one-per-line-name.f909: One per line, name = expression. Each name is replaced wherever it appears, in the circuit and in every other box. E.g. vx = va-vb, then use vx as a dependent source's value.
open-a-terminal-in.55d3: open a terminal in the folder and run sh start.sh
opens-the-equation-system.6075: opens the equation system in the Numerical Solver
or-take-the-answers.0d85: Or take the answers somewhere they can be worked on further: Export to SymPy writes them out as a small Python script, so every answer arrives as a SymPy expression you can expand, factor, substitute into or plot. Paste it into a Python prompt, a Jupyter notebook, or any online SymPy console.
partial-fractions-mdash-the.67c4: Partial fractions — the step before an inverse Laplace transform. It wants a single variable, so it suits an FD or TR answer in s rather than a DC one written in several resistors. 2/(s**2 + 3*s + 2) → 2/(s + 1) - 2/(s + 2)
powsimp-radsimp-trigsimp-log.667c: powsimp, radsimp, trigsimp, logcombine, cancel and diff are accepted too. They are narrower: diff(vo, v1) differentiates, and the rest gather powers, radicals, trig terms or logs, which a circuit answer rarely has enough of to notice.
prefer-to-do-it.ea57: Prefer to do it by hand? Open a terminal in the unzipped folder and run python3 -m http.server 8000, then visit http://localhost:8000/.
provide-additional-equations.ed5e: Provide additional equations, unknowns and/or conditions to be considered.
pulls-a-sum-of.5497: Pulls a sum of fractions over one denominator. v1/r1 + v2/r2 → (r1*v2 + r2*v1)/(r1*r2)
rms-phasors-off-means.e4c8: RMS phasors — off means peak amplitude (the ÷2 convention); affects AC power only
select-the-information-you.a36a: Select the information you want to export and download as a text file.
show-ac-answers-as.f2a8: Show AC answers as polar phasors — 3 + 4j becomes 5∠53.13°; average power stays real
show-equations-adds-an.b3d5: Show equations — adds an Equations card listing the system the solver assembled
show-units-in-answers.89ab: Show units in answers — V, A, W, VA, Ω
si-prefixes-apply-to.6c04: SI prefixes apply to numeric answers only; a symbolic answer such as x·vin/(r1 + x) is left as it is. A prefixed value is a decimal, so SI prefixes and exact can't both apply.
since-all-versions-of.c18e: Since 2013, all versions of Symbulator are offered under a Creative Commons License (CC) BY-NC-SA. Since 2026, all versions of Symbulator are free and open-source software, released under the MIT licence: you may use, study, modify and share it, including commercially, with attribution. The solver is published as the symbulator package on PyPI, and the project for it and this interface lives on GitHub. Contributions, bug reports and circuits that break it are welcome.
symbulator-is-a-free.2be5: Symbulator is a free linear circuit simulator for handheld devices. The name is a portmanteau of "symbolic simulator": Symbulator accepts inputs with numerical and symbolic values, and provides numerical and symbolic results. Over a quarter of a century, Symbulator has been widely considered the best symbolic simulator of linear circuits ever made for a handheld device. Symbulator is, has always been and will always be free of cost. Acknowledgements
symbulator-speaks-thirteen-l.5bee: Symbulator speaks thirteen languages, and every translation was written by an AI rather than by someone who speaks the language. If you read one of them, correcting a phrase is the most useful thing you can do for this program. The dictionaries are files you can take away, edit and send back. Help translate Symbulator
symbulator-was-made-by.4a2e: Symbulator was made by Roberto Perez-Franco on a Texas Instruments TI-89 calculator, starting in 1999, as an engineering student at Universidad Tecnológica de Panamá (UTP). An early version won 1st place at the 2000 IEEE Student Paper Contest for Latin America. Version 5 served as Roberto's graduation thesis in 2001. He released version 6 in 2013 and version 7 in 2023, both for the TI-89 Titanium, along with a port to the TI-Nspire CAS II as version 8.

the-best-portable-symbolic.4e2c: the best portable symbolic simulator of linear circuits
the-first-letter-of.80e2: The first letter of an element's name selects its type. Element letters, element names and node names are not case-sensitive: R1 and r1 are the same resistor, and node A is node a.
the-solver-opens-in.487d: The solver opens in a new tab, preloaded with this solve’s equations and results. From there:
this-copy-of-the.6df3: 🧭 This copy of the page can't reach a maths engine, so the calculator can't run from here. You can still use Symbulator by running it entirely inside your own browser instead — see “Run locally” near the bottom of this page, or go straight to install.symbulator.com.
this-online-version-of.83ca: This online version of Symbulator 9 is hosted remotely and needs an internet connection every time you use it. There is an identical offline version that runs entirely inside your own browser — nothing is sent to any server — so once you've downloaded it, it keeps working with no internet at all, and your browser can install it like an ordinary app.
this-port-of-symbulator.5ea6: This port of Symbulator to Python and SymPy is version 9 in that lineage. Whereas versions 1 through 8 were written by Roberto entirely by hand, this new version — in a sign of the times — was ported and developed using Anthropic's AI assistant. Claude took care of all the coding, while Roberto provided instructions and feedback, during an intense collaboration in August 2026. It is the author's hope that this port will preserve Symbulator for a new generation.
this-process-requires-python.095b: This process requires Python 3 only to run the one-time local server above — get it free from python.org if you don't have it; nothing else needs installing, since the maths engine itself (Python, SymPy and the symbulator package) runs inside your browser.
this-system-is-too.d20f: This system is too large to travel in a link, so it was saved as numerical_system.json — drop that file anywhere on the Numerical Solver page that just opened, and it loads.
this-will-start-a.e391: This will start a small local web server and open Symbulator 9 in your browser automatically. Leave that window open while you use the software.
tr-reads-a-source.8987: TR reads a source value as a function of time: 12 is a 12 V step, u(t) the unit step, t a ramp, δ(t) an impulse. The Greek letter is hard to type, so delta(t) is read exactly the same as δ(t). FD reads it in the s-domain instead: 5/s is a 5 V step and 5 an impulse. To write an FD source in time, wrap it — {5}, {u(t)} — which is shorthand for t2s(…) and works in FD only.
translate-a-circuit-between.caba: Translate a circuit between Symbulator notation and a SPICE netlist (ngspice, LTspice, PSpice). Whatever the destination notation cannot express is reported below and left out, rather than mistranslated. This translator is in beta — check the translated circuit before relying on it.
two-links-below-the.2eaf: Two links below the circuit box put the inputs you have on screen into the open file, and only one of them shows at a time: Save inputs to new entry adds them as a new entry, and Update inputs in this entry overwrites the entry you are already working in.
unknown-s-to-solve.bc0e: Unknown(s) to solve for — one per line or separated by commas, e.g. vx or v_x; leave blank to solve for whatever is left
untick-an-equation-flip.5a8d: Untick an equation, flip a Known to Unknown, and watch the results follow.
upload-an-input-file.b4e3: Upload an input file of circuit entries
upload-at-the-top.4b33: Upload, at the top of this card, reads a file like the one above: its entries become the input file open in your browser, replacing whatever was open before. The file is only read, never stored. Download, beside it, writes the open file back out, and is available whenever that file has at least one entry in it.
use-si-prefixes-in.3ef1: Use SI prefixes in answers — 0.002 becomes 2 m, 1200 becomes 1.2 k
what-results-are-you.b148: What results are you after? List the variables here: e.g. v_2, i_l1
what-to-include-saved.52b3: What to include — saved as an Output File
what-you-can-do.cbc5: What you can do with itWhat it does
when-conducting-an-ac.4fb7: When conducting an AC analysis, or an analysis in the AC mode, i, I, j and J all mean the imaginary unit and cannot be used as variable names — write 3j, 3*j or 3*i and you get the same thing, shown as 3j. Outside AC, those four letters are ordinary variable names like any other. pi is π. Every other name you write is an ordinary variable, so Q, S and beta mean what you intend rather than something out of SymPy. Euler's number is exp(1).
when-the-app-writes.39e9: When the app writes a file it puts the keys in the order shown above — element lines, then the analysis type and Expert Mode, then Settings, then Evaluate, Solve equations and Plot. Nothing that reads a file back in cares about that order, so a hand-written file can put them wherever is convenient.
works-on-mobile-devices.8ab6: Works on mobile devices, Windows, macOS and Linux. To install a local copy directly from a browser, visit install.symbulator.com. That page offers an Install button of its own — tap it and confirm, and you are done.
works-on-windows-macos.b9b9: Works on Windows, macOS and Linux. The same offline version is also published as a single .zip of about 30 MB — useful when there is no internet to install from, when it has to travel by USB stick or over a local network, or simply to keep a copy that will go on working whatever happens to this site. Unzip it anywhere and open the launcher inside: download the .zip.
write-the-apostrophe-k.c85a: Write the apostrophe — 1'k — to say plainly that you mean an SI prefix. A bare 1k also works, but it is ambiguous (one kilo, or one times a variable named k?) and Symbulator will stop and ask.
